Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. Have you ever noticed how, in everyday conversations, some voices seem to matter more than others? Sometimes it's subtle, other times it's glaringly obvious, but there's this invisible pecking order that shapes who gets listened to, who gets doubted, and who gets to be the so-called "expert."
As we dive into Men Explain Things to Me, guided by Rebecca Solnit’s powerful voice, we’ll start to see how those little moments—when a story is brushed aside, a fact is doubted, or a woman is talked over—aren’t just one-offs. They’re part of a bigger pattern, a quiet but persistent current of gendered power that flows through our lives, in both intimate spaces and out in the world.
Together, we’ll explore how these experiences build up, shaping a wider story about who’s allowed to speak, who’s believed, and whose stories really count. Solnit’s essays connect the dots between personal moments and the bigger social picture, showing us that these issues aren’t just about individual behavior—they’re about systems and structures that touch everything from our closest relationships to the institutions we rely on.
So, what does it really mean to listen? How do we find the courage to speak up—and make sure every voice gets its turn? This journey invites us to look at the familiar in a new light, and together, we’ll uncover why making space for every story isn’t just important—it’s urgent.
